notes: Identity independently checked: title Implicit Theories of Intelligence Predict Achievement Across an Adolescent Transition: A Longitudinal Study and an Intervention; authors Lisa S. Blackwell, Kali H. Trzesniewski, Carol Sorich Dweck; Child Development, January/February 2007, Volume 78, Number 1, Pages 246–263. Wiley header identifies DOI 10.1111/j.1467-8624.2007.00995.x. This is a primary article with Study 1 methods/results, Study 2, references and appendices, not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF supplied. Page-6 locator and change-in-grades description identify the HLM theory-by-time slope effect .53, t = 2.93, p < .05. Canonical text renders the symbol as b; standardised-beta identity is not established, so no conversion or standardisation claim is made. Distinct candidates outside this target: p. 251 endpoint regressions .17 and .10 with different covariates; p. 252 single-factor mediation theory effects .20 before and .11 after the mediator. Study 1 overall participant count is 373; Figure 2 explicitly reports N = 373 for a separate SEM process model. Neither establishes an explicit analytic N for the target HLM or endpoint regressions. Target-test exclusions are not specified. No N sum or df-based derivation performed. Unassigned replication and success fields are placeholders.
